transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

That's almost always a broken drive belt. The motor spins, but with no belt nothing connects it to the drum. It's one of the most common dryer faults and usually a cheap DIY fix.

## Quick check (2 minutes)
1. Unplug the dryer.
2. Open the door and turn the drum by hand.
• Spins very freely with almost no resistance → belt is almost certainly snapped.
• Feels normal/stiff → belt may be intact but slipping, or it's the tension pulley (see below).

## Likely causes, most to least common
1. Snapped or stretched belt. The usual culprit. A new belt costs about £10-20 / $10-25.
2. Worn or seized idler (tension) pulley. This keeps the belt tight. If its spring breaks or the wheel seizes, the belt goes slack and slips. You'll often hear squealing or grinding beforehand.
3. Worn motor pulley. Less common.
4. Overloading. A very heavy wet load can make a worn belt slip.

## Fixing it
• Find your model number. It's usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back. Order the belt for that exact model, since sizes vary.
• Replace the idler pulley at the same time. It's cheap, and a worn one often causes the belt to fail.
• Search YouTube for "Hotpoint [your model number] belt replacement." There's usually a video for your exact model.
• Typical job: remove the top or front panel, loop the new belt around the drum (ribbed side down), then thread it under the idler pulley and around the motor pulley. Allow 30-60 minutes for a first-timer. The fiddly part is getting the belt tensioned correctly around the pulleys.

## Safety
• Always unplug first. If it's a gas dryer, also turn off the gas.
• Stop running it. Running the motor with no drum movement won't help, and it can strain things or overheat.

Tip: While the panel is off, vacuum out the lint inside the cabinet. It builds up and is a fire risk.

ive turned the drum by hand with it unplugged and it spins really easy almost no resistance. model starts TVHM8 but the rest of the sticker is worn off. heard a twang then thud yesterday mid cycle and a slight rubber smell at the time

That confirms it: your drive belt has snapped. The twang was the belt breaking, the thud was it dropping inside the cabinet, and the rubber smell was likely the belt slipping or rubbing before it failed. A drum that spins with almost no resistance is the giveaway.

## Getting the right belt without the full model number
TVHM8... is a Hotpoint Aquarius-style 8kg vented dryer, but there are several variants, so try these:

1. Read the old belt itself. Once the panel is off, the snapped belt will be lying in the bottom. It almost always has its size printed on it, e.g. "1860 H7" or "1965 H7". The number is the length in mm, and H7 means 7 ribs. Order that exact size and you can't go wrong.
2. Check other places for the model number: the rating plate inside the door rim (sometimes there's a second sticker), the back panel, the manual, your receipt or online order history, or your Hotpoint registration if you registered it.
3. Give a parts supplier what you have. UK sites like eSpares or Partmaster can often narrow it down from "TVHM8" plus your photo or description, or from the serial number if any of that is readable.

Expect around £10-20 for the belt. Consider getting the idler (tension) pulley too, roughly £10-15. A snapped belt sometimes means the pulley was worn or seizing.

## While you're in there, check
• Idler pulley: it should spin freely and smoothly, with no wobble, grinding, or flat spots, and the spring should be intact.
• Drum rollers/bearings at the back: if they're stiff or worn, they put extra load on the belt.
• Lint build-up in the cabinet: vacuum it out. Lint plus friction heat is a fire risk.
• Anything caught near the motor or drum, like a sock, coin, or underwire, that might have jammed the belt.

## The job, roughly
1. Unplug, and pull the dryer out so you can reach the back.
2. Remove the top panel. It's usually held by screws at the back; slide it back and lift.
3. Access to the belt varies on these models, often via the front panel. Search YouTube for "Hotpoint Aquarius TVHM80 belt replacement". There are good videos for this range.
4. Loop the new belt around the drum, ribbed side facing in, toward the drum, roughly where the old wear mark is.
5. Thread it around the idler pulley and the motor pulley so the pulley holds it tight. This is the fiddly bit and may take a few tries.
6. Before reassembling, turn the drum by hand. It should now have firm, even resistance and the belt should stay centred.

Allow about an hour for a first attempt.

If you find a number on the old belt, or any more of the model number, send it over and I'll help you confirm the right part.
